---
title: "Module 2: Synchronization and Collective Behaviour"
subtitle: "Syllabus Part II"
format: html
---

This module studies how order appears in large groups of interacting units. You start with one oscillator on the circle and one oscillator driven by a rhythm, move to the Kuramoto model of many coupled oscillators and the Millennium Bridge, and end with models of flocks, schools and crowds. The main tools are phase equations, order parameters and agent-based simulation [@strogatz2024nonlinear; @strogatz2000kuramoto; @vicsek1995novel].

# Learning Goals

By the end of this module you should be able to:

- Describe an oscillator by its phase and analyse flows on the circle, including the saddle-node bifurcation of the nonuniform oscillator.
- Derive the locking range of an oscillator driven by a periodic stimulus.
- Write the Kuramoto model, rewrite it in mean-field form, and state the critical coupling $K_c = 2/(\pi g(0))$.
- Simulate the Kuramoto model, measure $r_\infty(K)$, and separate real synchronization from finite-size fluctuations.
- Explain the Millennium Bridge instability as a feedback loop between crowd synchrony and bridge motion, and compute the critical crowd size.
- Implement the Vicsek model and explain the roles of noise and density in the transition to collective motion.
- Compare the rules and the questions of the Vicsek, Couzin and social force models.
